Tidy an mvgam object's parameter posteriors

Source: R/tidier_methods.R
tidy.mvgam.Rd

Posterior summaries of the parameters of a fitted mvgam model, as a tibble with the columns of broom.mixed: term, estimate, std.error, conf.low and conf.high. A type column assigns each parameter to the observation model or the trend.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
tidy(
  x,
  effects = "all",
  robust = FALSE,
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  rhat = FALSE,
  ess = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam object.

effects

"all" (the default) for every parameter, or one of "fixed", "ran_pars" and "ran_vals" for the categories above, as in broom.mixed::tidy.brmsfit().

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

conf.int

Logical. If TRUE (the default), include conf.low and conf.high posterior quantile columns.

conf.level

Numeric. Probability covered by the credible interval reported in conf.low / conf.high. Defaults to 0.95.

rhat

Logical. If TRUE, add a rhat column with posterior::rhat() values.

ess

Logical. If TRUE, add an ess_bulk column with posterior::ess_bulk() values.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

Value

A tibble with one row per parameter and the columns term, type, estimate and std.error. conf.int = TRUE adds conf.low and conf.high. rhat and ess add rhat and ess_bulk.

Details

The type column places every parameter into one of the following categories, each with the effects class it belongs to:

  • "observation_family_extra_param" (ran_pars) – auxiliary observation-family parameters such as sigma, shape, nu, phi, zi, hu.

  • "observation_beta" (fixed) – population-level coefficients of the observation formula, with the intercept and the fixed parts of its smooths and monotonic terms.

  • "observation_smooth_param" (ran_pars) – the penalty of each smooth (sds_) and the marginal deviation and length scale of each Gaussian process.

  • "observation_smooth_coef" (ran_vals) – the penalised basis coefficients of the smooths and Gaussian processes.

  • "random_effect_group_level" (ran_pars) – the standard deviations and correlations of the observation formula's group-level terms.

  • "random_effect_beta" (ran_vals) – the group-level coefficients themselves, one per level and term.

  • "trend_model_param" (ran_pars) – parameters of the trend dynamics (ar1_trend, theta1_trend, Sigma_trend, k_trend, m_trend, delta_trend, etc.) and the factor loadings.

  • "trend_beta", "trend_smooth_param", "trend_smooth_coef", "trend_random_effect_group_level" and "trend_random_effect_beta" – the same five blocks of the trend formula.

Fixed-effect terms take the names fixef.mvgam() gives them, as broom.mixed::tidy.brmsfit() names them: b_x is x and b_sigma_x is sigma_x. Every other term keeps the name variables.mvgam() lists. brms samples a centred intercept and transforms it to the intercept on the data's scale. The table reports the coefficient once, as Intercept.

See also

Other tidiers: augment.mvgam(), glance.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# One row per parameter, with broom's column names
td <- tidy(mod)
td
#> # A tibble: 8 × 6
#>   term                  type               estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>                 <chr>                 <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 Intercept             observation_beta    1.63       0.139     1.34      1.91 
#> 2 sx_1                  observation_beta    8.48       2.34      3.68     13.0  
#> 3 sds_sx_1              observation_smoot…  5.14       1.98      2.37      9.97 
#> 4 s_sx_1[1]             observation_smoot…  1.44       1.78     -1.99      5.14 
#> 5 s_sx_1[2]             observation_smoot…  0.00553    2.04     -4.06      4.11 
#> 6 s_sx_1[3]             observation_smoot… -8.44       1.69    -11.7      -5.02 
#> 7 sigma_trend[series_1] trend_model_param   0.470      0.0716    0.337     0.624
#> 8 ar1_trend[series_1]   trend_model_param   0.565      0.144     0.254     0.814

# The `type` column separates the trend's parameters from the
# observation model's
td[td$type == "trend_model_param", ]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   term                  type              estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>                 <chr>                <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 sigma_trend[series_1] trend_model_param    0.470    0.0716    0.337     0.624
#> 2 ar1_trend[series_1]   trend_model_param    0.565    0.144     0.254     0.814

# The fixed effects alone, with convergence diagnostics
tidy(mod, effects = "fixed", rhat = TRUE, ess = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   term      type            estimate std.error conf.low conf.high  rhat ess_bulk
#>   <chr>     <chr>              <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 Intercept observation_be…     1.63     0.139     1.34      1.91  1.00    1075.
#> 2 sx_1      observation_be…     8.48     2.34      3.68     13.0   1.00     831.

# Next, augment() adds fitted values and residuals to the data
# }
